name: Reunification and child welfare
description: Expertise for reuniting children with families and for child welfare continuity in a disaster: the plan and site layout, roster, release log, parent text, call script, unreleased student tracker, displaced children list, state plan activation notice and crisis counseling request.
outsideParties: the national missing and exploited children center

advisorRoles.name: Reunification advisor
advisorRoles.description: Answers questions about site flow, roles and release authority as a school safety director would.

advisorRoles.name: Child welfare disaster advisor
advisorRoles.description: Answers questions about locating children in care and the state disaster plan.

glossary.definition: Check-in (verify the guardian), retrieval (bring the student), release (hand over and log), exceptions (cases that do not fit). Release authority is verified by identity.

State plans cover how the state identifies, locates and continues services for children displaced by a disaster, responds to new cases in the area and stays in contact with displaced staff (Social Security Act title IV-B, 42 U.S.C. 622(b)(16)).
FEMA funds crisis counseling in presidentially declared disasters (Stafford Act section 416, 44 CFR 206.171): immediate services up to 60 days, regular services up to nine months.

productConventions: Students and children are exercise references (S-017, C-0412), never names; status words are written out (RELEASED, PENDING, EXCEPTION, LOCATED, UNKNOWN).
Roster, release log and summary counts must add up to the roster total.
Name trademarked school reunification methods only as references; do not copy their forms.
realismRules: Release only to a guardian on the release card verified by photo identification; no release by phone.
Parents arrive faster than staff can verify; rumors name the wrong site; plan for both.
No student is left alone; a student with no guardian reached goes to the commander, counselors and social services under district policy.

criticalTasks: Activate the reunification site with named roles and a single release authority
Release every student only to a verified guardian and log each release
Handle exceptions and unreleased students without leaving a student alone
Identify and locate every displaced child in care within the plan targets
Continue hotline intake and visits from temporary sites
Request crisis counseling immediate services for affected communities
